readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. A Read has TWO ceilings — it
TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB — and BOTH HAVE ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE.
iter127 hit the byte ceiling: the Read was refused at 459 KB, 397 KB of it the `done` log. iter128
found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and unnoticed, returning lines 1-43 of 92 and
dropping `decisions`, `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT (corrected iter129): the tool prints an explicit "[Truncated: PARTIAL view]"
notice, so the risk is an agent SKIMMING PAST it, not the tool hiding anything. How the B/tok
constants were derived moved to method-notes.md at iter160; check_calibration owns them now.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO
PLAN.md. It measures ALL THREE step-1 files, prints each one's HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates,
distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields, flags every other tools/loop file,
and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting. WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy
field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents
— `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`, `methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`,
`spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one keeping its pointer INSIDE the field it
drained) and `doneRecent` (iter151, drained to empty; see `doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) —
and each asserted its round-trip before this file was rewritten. DO NOT DISCARD CONTENT TO MAKE THE
CHECK PASS: condensing prose you keep is fair payback, dropping archived text is not. WHEN IT TRIPS
ON GATES.md OR PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled
section, never drop one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. **ITER179: A NEW SEAM - THE `--dry-run` PROMISE, PLACEMENT-ENFORCED PER COMMAND EXACTLY AS THE WRITE LOCK IS.** Account: done-archive.jsonl:180.

  **THE POPULATION WAS ALREADY ENUMERATED BY SOMEBODY ELSE.** `WriteLockCoverageTests.Callers` lists the five files reaching a Confluence write, so auditing a SECOND placement-enforced rule cost a read of rule A's list, not a fresh trace. **FOUR OF FIVE WERE COVERED** - publish, dashboard, drift --mark. **THE FIFTH WAS NOT:** `sync --reply` is the only sync half that writes to Confluence (SyncCommand.cs:412 says so), and the one sync dry-run test covers the INGESTION half, whose writes are all in the repo; `--labels` writes nothing anywhere. The flag was asserted on every sync path but the only one that can POST.

  Shipped `A_reply_dry_run_posts_nothing_and_stamps_no_item`: exit 0, plan printed, `Writes()` empty, item unstamped. Both write stubs are registered on purpose - why is in the test's own remarks. **HARNESS 4/4, restore byte-IDENTICAL, git clean**; the mutate-the-POLICY cell (keep the `--dry-run` message, drop only `return 0;`) CAUGHT, proving the write-footprint assertion carries the test. **BOTH RED CELLS FAILED EXACTLY 1 OF 1426 - THE NEW TEST IS THE SOLE DETECTOR.** Verified: build 0/0; suite **1426 skipped=0**. **`EXPECTED_AT_LEAST` 1425 -> 1426.** Nothing decided, no gate moved, nothing pushed.
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE - NOT `dotnet test | tail`**, which drops the failure lines above the summary (iter154). **Expect 1426**; run-suite.py enforces that floor, plus red on an unparseable summary or any skip. A DROP is the signal; a deliberate one means editing `EXPECTED_AT_LEAST` in the same commit and saying why (iter179: 1425->1426). Several tests sweep the tree's own PROSE outside `tests/`/`tools/`, so a docs-only edit - GATES.md too - can turn it red, and **in C# a DOC COMMENT is prose too.** Reword it; **never widen a tripwire's count to fit prose.** **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1** (iter172); one class is `--filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, **ONE pattern, and a path naming a single METHOD collects zero**. **AND `cd` PERSISTS BETWEEN Bash CALLS** (iter178).

**ONE MEASURED ITEM IS OPEN AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A TRACE: `publish --prune --dry-run` is NEVER INVOKED by the suite, and its exit code is HOST-DEPENDENT** - PruneGuard reads the CI vars (PruneGuard.cs:71) before PublishCommand's `!dryRun` conjunct (:342), so CI refuses it and a laptop proceeds. Ship the weak test, add a seam, or leave it recorded. **DO NOT RE-MEASURE - account: `--find 179`.**

**SEAMS SPENT, iters 157-179, DO NOT RE-PROBE: the checker layer, the orientation layer, `WikiTree.InScope`, the unreferenced-asset invariant, the whole-tree-abort family, publish/prune cancellation, feedback cancellation, the client's pagination layer, ALL THREE durable-write layers, and the dry-run promise on all five write surfaces.** A new increment must name a NEW seam. **THE METHOD GENERALISES AND IS THE CHEAPEST LEAD LEFT: when one placement-enforced rule has a coverage test, ITS pinned surface list is the population for auditing every OTHER rule of that shape** - `WriteLockCoverageTests` and `PruneConfirmationCoverageTests` are the two.

**DO THE BOOKKEEPING BEFORE run-harnesses.py - ITER170 BURNED A ~7-MINUTE SWEEP ON THIS.** A half-finished state.json fails six guards at once and no message says so - `iteration` ahead of `doneCount` reddens `check_done_archive`, and every harness using the checker as BASELINE aborts. Order: archive line, `doneCount`, `phase`/`nextAction`, THEN sweep - and **do not edit state.json while a sweep is in flight** (iter171).

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`. AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** (iter155). **AND `git log --oneline -5` AGAINST `iteration`** (iter169: two commits this file did not mention). **Trust `decisions`/`gates` plus GATES.md's checkboxes over prose here; this prose can be flatly WRONG, not just stale** (iter170). **RUN THE TOOL BEFORE SPENDING AN ITERATION ON A NUMBER HERE.**

**A GREEN LOCAL BUILD IS NOT A GREEN CI (iter169).** `gh run list --limit 3` is part of verification whenever anything reaches origin: CI resolves a newer SDK and `AnalysisLevel: latest-recommended` follows it, so 0 warnings here can be N errors there (`decisions.analyzerBandDrift`). **DO NOT "FIX" IT** - ToolchainPinningTests asserts the hazard is still there. **origin/main is 12 BEHIND** as of iter179, so CI has never run on any of them; no standing push authority - `decisions.pushPolicy`.

**`python3 tools/loop/run-harnesses.py` (10/10, ~7 min) RE-CHECKS EVERY SEAM ITERS 157-170 TOUCHED, naming them as it runs. THE CHECKER SEAM IS SPENT: DO NOT RE-PROBE IT.** A product-code harness stays in `.mtk/` scratch, NOT in `HARNESSES` (that list guards this tooling); iters 113/173-179 all did, guarantee carried by the tests.

**BUDGET - READ BEFORE WRITING A METHOD NOTE. method-notes.md IS AT ~19,960 OF 20,000 TOKENS: 40 TOKENS, EFFECTIVELY ZERO.** iter179 wanted a note and **did not force one at the end of an iteration** - funding it is an INDEXING PASS, its own increment and a legitimate one to pick. **THE ONLY LEVER THAT MEASURED WELL IS REWRITING A VERBOSE STUB AS AN INDEX** - iters 173/175 indexed TWO to fund a section, iter176 THREE, iter177 SIX; that is the going rate. **Rotation and boilerplate are BOTH spent.** Otherwise: WRITE LESS, and **put the size assertion in the write script so it refuses you** - iters 176/178/179 each had theirs do exactly that. Generations: method-notes.md's own header. **A generation 4 must be declared in BOTH `ARCHIVE_FILES` and `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS` in the same change - a FAILING CHECK, not advice.** **THIS FILE IS TIGHTER STILL:** a new `phase`/`nextAction` must be no larger than the pair it replaces.

**EVERY REMAINING PLAN.md SS15 ITEM IS GATED ON MIRKO:** ten boxes, EIGHT decisions.

**check-state-size.py RUNS TWELVE CHECKS** and nine refuse a vacuous pass. **FIVE DECLARED LISTS MUST BE EDITED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS WHAT THEY DECLARE:** `GATES_ARCHIVE_NON_GATE_KEYS`, `ARCHIVE_FILES`, `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS`, `CITATION_KNOWN_ABSENT`, **`HARNESSES` paired BOTH ways with the runner's STEPS**. **SETTLING A BLOCKER IS A FOUR-PLACE EDIT** (iter160); the fourth - the body into blockers-archive.jsonl - is the only one whose omission DESTROYS text (iter155 skipped it). **ROTATING A METHOD NOTE IS A THREE-PLACE EDIT** (iter166). **A REFUSAL APPENDS, IT NEVER `return`s** (iter165). **DO NOT WRITE SPECIMEN PATHS IN PROSE** (iter167): path-shaped prose must resolve on disk; the gitignored-.mtk ratchet reads 17 of 21.

**A CONSTANT IN PROSE IS A MIRROR.** `check_prose_constants` fails on a bytes-per-token ratio neither live nor dated. **Live pair: 2.4 B/tok markdown, 2.3 JSON - never copy undated.**

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. TEN BOXES ARE UNCHECKED, ALL MIRKO'S** - five milestone gates, five side items, mirrored in `gates`; **the checker FAILS ON MIRROR OR STATUS DRIFT**, so trust it. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver, m3, m4, m5, m2, m6. **EIGHT DECISIONS ARE OPEN, ALL FULLY MEASURED - DO NOT REDO THAT WORK.** What is left is a JUDGEMENT the loop must not make.

**paste-format-on-edit-hook'S QUESTION IS SETTLED - DO NOT RE-ASK, DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`** (check #10 FAILS if it reappears). **The loop cannot write `.claude/`**: do not retry, do not route around it with `python3`. **tools/loop/docume-loop.sh CAN BE EDITED BUT CANNOT TAKE EFFECT** - bash parses a `while` once and the driver started 2026-07-24, so a "fix" is committed and not running (`gates.restart-loop-driver`, 9/9 at iter140, NOTHING PENDING). Live, re-read by path each pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md, loop-settings.json.

**MUTATION-HARNESS RULES LIVE IN tools/loop/method-notes.md** (`methodNotes.appendHere`) - read it whole first. **A HEREDOC IS REFUSED**: a one-shot script goes in a file under `.mtk/paths-<n>/`, **and so does an inline `python3 -c` carrying a `#` comment** (iter178). iter170: a PARTIAL mutation grades the CHECK broken. iter171: `rm -rf` IS DENIED; use `shutil.rmtree`. **iter173: A BUILD FAILURE CAN SCORE *GREEN*** - match `error [A-Z]+\d+` case-insensitively, and **mutate the CALL SITE, since deleting a failure path orphans its variables**. **iter174/178: A MISSED OR GREEN CELL CAN BE THE BEST FINDING.** **iter175: A ZERO-TEST RUN SCORES GREEN TOO** - assert the DENOMINATOR, carry a must-stay-GREEN control. **iter176/179: revert via `git show HEAD:<file>`, and A PREDICTED VERDICT YOUR GRADER CANNOT EMIT IS A BUG IN THE GRADER** - iter179 scored 2/4 because its TRX names were fully qualified and its predictions bare; fix the grader and re-run. **iter177: PREDICT A FAILURE SET, NEVER A COUNT** - and **iter179: A RED CELL FAILING EXACTLY ONE TEST IS ITSELF THE FINDING** (sole detector = total gap).

**HYGIENE, DO NOT DELETE WITHOUT ASKING** (a data file): untracked `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json`, harmless since iters 171-172 but still copied into both build outputs every build. Ask Mirko: delete or gitignore? **A FLAKE RECURRED AT ITER179, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME** (iter168's was logged twice as UNNAMED): `ConfluenceClientTests.A_rate_limited_create_is_replayed_with_the_same_body`, WireMock 404 on `api/v2/pages`, once post-commit then **3/3 green**. Not a find yet; twice IN A ROW is.

blockers._archive: FULL BLOCKER BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/blockers-open.json (moved at iter139; nothing discarded, round-trip asserted — the eighth archive precedent, and like decisions._archive the pointer stays INSIDE the field it drained). Each line below is ONE OPEN blocker: what it is, whose call it is, and where to answer. EVERY ONE IS PHRASED AS A QUESTION FOR MIRKO and every one is also written up at length in GATES.md, which step 1 reads anyway — so open the archive only to ACT on one. NOTE: tools/loop/blockers-archive.jsonl is a DIFFERENT file holding SETTLED blockers. **`blockers` IS AN OBJECT, NOT AN ARRAY** (matching `gates` and `decisions`; nothing reads it programmatically — checked). TO ADD ONE, per protocol step 9: a short kebab-case key here with a ONE-LINE stub ending in a pointer, and the full body in blockers-open.json under the same key. TO SETTLE ONE, **FOUR PLACES, AND check-state-size.py NOW FAILS ON A HALF-EDIT**: delete the key from both, append a one-line verdict to blockersArchive.settled, AND append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl (line shape: `blockersArchive.format`). **THE FOURTH DESTROYS CONTENT IF SKIPPED** - iter155 skipped it. (Condensed iter150 as budget payback; the historical justification for the iter139 move is in blockers-open.json and the done archive.)
blockers.pushPolicy: OPEN, ITER121 — **may the loop push to origin/main?** The same question as `decisions.pushPolicy` in this file, which carries the numbers and the iter130 note; answer it THERE ("always", "on-request" or "never"). Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading; blocks no offline work. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.rule-8-2a: OPEN, ITER75 — **may the §8.2a rule amendment be pasted?** One paste of tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md into .claude/rules/git-workflow.md beneath §8.2. It scopes the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete that work. The loop will not do it itself: it WIDENS force-push authority. Nothing waits on it. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json; full text GATES.md -> paste-rule-8-2a.
blockers.force-push-hook: OPEN, ITER130 — **may the force-push guard be installed?** One paste of tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md over tools/loop/loop-settings.json. §8.2 is labelled [ENFORCED] but its deny list only covers the flag-first spelling: `git push <remote> HEAD --force` and `--force-with-lease` were both measured ALLOWED. Fix is the committed PreToolUse hook tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, 25/25, and PROVEN TO LOAD AND FIRE FROM A --settings FILE at iter131, 3/3, without installing anything. **CONFIRMED ITER139: needs NO driver restart** — the running driver re-reads loop-settings.json by path every pass. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.settings-corrections: OPEN, ITER131, TWO ONE-LINERS, NEITHER BLOCKING ANYTHING — (a) this workspace is untrusted (~/.claude.json hasTrustDialogAccepted:false), so three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries are ignored every iteration; zero cost today because --settings supplies a broader rule. (b) `Write(.env)` / `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce NOTHING — only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. Both found by reading the CLI's own stderr, captured unread into every iteration log for 130 iterations. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.restart-loop-driver: OPEN, ITER139 — **will you restart the loop driver?** `touch tools/loop/STOP` -> wait for the pass to end -> `rm tools/loop/STOP` -> `./tools/loop/docume-loop.sh`. The running process started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once, so it is 56.6 h older than docume-loop.sh's newest commit and BOTH commits since (c6fbf1e; 7de6a86, iter137's entire deliverable) have never executed. tools/loop/MODEL is inert for the same reason. NOT blocking the pastes. ITER140: what the restart activates is now TESTED 9/9 and correct (.mtk/paths-140/probe-restart-readiness.py), and the only behaviour change it makes is the model ID string, measured harmless. Probe: .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py, 8/8. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.

gates.authoritative: GATES.md. It is richer than anything here and step 1 of the protocol tells you to read it; this block is the status mirror rule §9.7 asks for, not a second copy. The full pre-iter128 mirror text is in tools/loop/gates-archive.json.
gates.gate-m1-aurservices-files: CLOSED WITHOUT ACTION 2026-07-25 by Mirko ('just use your golden set'); M1 closed at iter48 (bcf36ba). DO NOT REOPEN — real-corpus validation moved to M7. Struck through in GATES.md with the full reasoning; verbatim mirror in tools/loop/gates-archive.json.
gates.gate-m2-aur-review: PENDING, MIRKO'S. The loop's half finished at iter113: 44 pages are up in DOCUMESBX. Needs your page-by-page review, then the tick. Caveat GATES.md states: cases/mermaid.md is deliberately absent (beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 rejects `graph TD;` and `pie`, and a page fails as a unit) - tick on the rendering you CAN see; the mermaid question is decisions.mermaidDialectGap, not this gate.
gates.gate-m3-approval-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the cheapest of the five: add ONE `approved` label to any published page ('CLI Reference', id 451969089, is a good one), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --labels`, republishes that page with `publish --notify-reviewers`, and you re-approve. `approvedBy` will read 'unknown' and that is correct, not a bug (spike S3: Confluence exposes no label author). THIS GATE ALSO GATES SHIPPED CODE - iter122's `--notify-reviewers` fires only where a run revokes an approval, and no DOCUMESBX page carries one, so nothing can exercise it live until this box moves.
gates.gate-m4-feedback-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S. Write ONE comment saying something factually wrong about a published page (an INLINE comment on a sentence exercises the most code), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --comments` -> `/docs-feedback` -> a `docs/feedback-<date>` PR -> republish -> `sync --reply`.
gates.gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and it is a DECISION not a task: does M5's §14 acceptance run on this repo (copy docs-drift-pr.yml in, add secrets) or fold into M7 where a real repo with real PRs exists? Answer in decisions.m5Acceptance. The live middle of the chain is already done and re-runnable (iter121: `drift --mark` labelled 9 of 11 sourced pages against DOCUMESBX and proved a label spends no page version).
gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm Directory.Build.props <Version>, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version and plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref all read the number you want (all three read 0.1.0; release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) delete the 'Not published yet' note from README.md; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance. A PAT with read:packages in the loop environment is needed for the install half.
gates.paste-rule-8-2a: PENDING, MIRKO'S, ONE PASTE, NOTHING WAITS ON IT — and it was missing from this block from iter75 to iter144, which is why check-state-size.py now derives this mirror from GATES.md. Add the §8.2a bullet to .claude/rules/git-workflow.md directly beneath §8.2, leaving §8.2 itself untouched; the exact text is verbatim in tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md below the `---`. The loop will not write it even though an allowlisted python3 could: it WIDENS force-push authority, which is what the guard in the way exists to prevent. Full reasoning: GATES.md. decisions._archive: FULL DECISION BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/decisions-archive.json, moved there at iter130 because this field was 11.6 KB of the 50 KB that put step 1's Read past its budget. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED and the round-trip was asserted before this file was rewritten (the seventh precedent, after doneArchive, blockersArchive, gatesArchive, methodNotes, scratchInventory and spikesArchive). Each key below is a one-line summary: what the decision is, whose call it is, and what to strike off which test when it is settled. `nextAction` carries the same list in the order worth settling, so orientation costs no extra Read; open the archive only to ACT on one. MIRKO: write your answer straight over the stub in this file — the key is what matters, not the text it replaces.
decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is his; the FACTS were fully measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else. Options: (a) upgrade-or-replace, (b) strip a trailing `;` in tools/render-mermaid.mjs, (c) report unsupported dialects as a named degradation instead of failing the page. iter156's four findings — 1.1.3 IS `dist-tags.latest`, so (a) means REPLACE or nothing; the gap is 17 diagram types and not 1; the semicolon rejection is an inconsistency INSIDE the library, which is what makes (b) cheap; and YAML frontmatter fails on every type including the six that work — moved to the body at iter162, verbatim, round-trip asserted. Full write-up: GATES.md's mermaid block. Body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.
decisions.m5Acceptance: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. Where M5's §14 acceptance runs: (a) install docs-drift-pr.yml here and open one PR (no secrets needed), (b) add secrets + docs-refresh/docs-publish, which makes every push to main publish to the sandbox, or (c) fold into M7 and reword §14. Also gate-m5. Interacts with pushPolicy. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json. **ITER157 MEASURED BOTH BUILDABLE OPTIONS AND NEITHER COSTS WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE: (a) IS ZERO-SECRET, AND (b) IS NARROWER THAN ITS DESCRIPTION** (docs-publish.yml is filtered to paths:['docs/wiki/**'], docs-refresh.yml is not push-triggered at all) — the numbers moved to the body at iter163, verbatim, round-trip asserted.
decisions.pushPolicy: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. May the loop `git push origin main`? Answer "always", "on-request" or "never". **ITER169: THE FACTS UNDER THIS QUESTION CHANGED. An interactive session pushed at f2308b4, so origin/main is CURRENT (0 ahead, 0 behind) — it was 107 behind at 699c855 when this was written — and CI now runs on every push.** That was an action taken with you present, NOT an answer: the loop still has no standing authority and will not push. It also settled the iter130 caveat in the loop's favour — the force-push guard is installed (gate paste-force-push-hook, DONE), so the hole this decision used to widen is closed. decisions.planSection6Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter122. §6's preamble declares three global options that did not ship as declared: `--verbose` built NOWHERE, `--json` built on `status` alone (`drift` spells it `--format`), `--config` absent from `init`/`convert`. Either BUILD them (three slices) or CORRECT §6. Then strike the entry off `UnbuiltOptions` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanCommandSpecTests.cs. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json. **ITER157: NOTHING SHIPPED DEPENDS ON THE THREE UNBUILT OPTIONS, so correcting §6 breaks no consumer and building them unblocks nothing that is asking** — already a standing assertion via CliReferencePageTests; the file-by-file measurement moved to the body at iter163, verbatim, round-trip asserted.
decisions.planSection5Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter123. Two config fields load, validate, round-trip and are read by NO line of src/: `links.repoBlobUrl` and `drift.defaultBranch`.
